faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium ROV Tether Swivel Joint suitable for ROV tether management system swivel joint?
faq.a: Titanium ROV Tether Swivel Joint uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address deep sea operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium ROV Tether Swivel Joint?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium ROV Tether Swivel Joint require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. deep sea components receive Heavy-duty passivation 25% HNO3 45min per ASTM B600 for maximum chloride pitting resistance in seawater. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the service environment.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium ROV Tether Swivel Joint shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements; (4) Surface roughness certification on critical features. FAIR available on request.

faq.q: What is the MOQ and typical lead time for Tether swivel / Cable joint deep sea components?
